title: reliability-lighthouse-initiative-tracker-for-sli-attribution-and-rollback
creator: Nora Patel
description: Create a lightweight 'Lighthouse' initiative tracker and attribution model to consolidate SLI/SLQ (service-level-quality) targets, per-service error budget consumption, and automated rollback gates. The Lighthouse will be used by PMs and SREs to make coordinated decisions when multiple services contribute to an SLI degradation and to standardize when and how rollouts are throttled or rolled back.
background: We have fragmented decks and spreadsheets tracking SLIs and error budgets per service. During recent incidents, teams lacked a single source-of-truth to attribute SLI drops to upstream vs serving-runtime regressions, which delayed rollback decisions. This initiative aims to centralize attribution signals, provide a simple UI for runbooks, and wire error-budget thresholds into rollout throttles in the Console.
goals: Surface per-route and per-model SLI trends with 24/7 error-budget burn alerts
Implement an attribution heuristic that surfaces likely root cause domains (runtime, model-regression, infra, network)
Ship a rollout-gate pattern: advisory -> throttle -> automatic rollback when error-budget crosses critical threshold
Provide an API for engineering to signal mitigations and for PMs to approve extended error-budget windows
success_criteria: Consolidated Lighthouse dashboard in Console with live SLI + error-budget view for 80% of high-traffic routes
Attribution heuristic correctly classifies root cause domain in >= 70% of past incidents in retrospective sample
Auto-rollbacks triggered in <5 minutes after critical threshold breach in a controlled canary experiment
Reduction in mean time to decision (MTTD) for rollout rollback from 42 minutes to <20 minutes in pilot teams
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard UI implemented with filter-by-route, filter-by-model, and error-budget health badges
Backend exposes a /lighthouse/attribution API with documented events and payloads (schema in docs link)
Rollout engine accepts a 'lighthouse_policy' flag and executes throttle/rollback actions when thresholds met
On-call runbook for the Lighthouse is published and linked from the dashboard
Demo run with two pilot services completes: attribution visible and auto-throttle exercised
tasks: Design: Lighthouse dashboard mockups and mobile-responsive fallback (DES-241)
Backend: telemetry aggregation pipeline for SLI + bucketed error-budget (ENG-6721)
Attribution: implement heuristic combining trace-error-rates, kv-cache hit drift, and model-quality deltas (ENG-6742)
Rollout: add 'lighthouse_policy' to rollout config and implement throttle/rollback hooks (ENG-6810)
Console: add action buttons to mute alerts, mark mitigations, and attach runbook notes (ENG-6889)
PM: run pilot with Payments and Search service owners; collect feedback and refine thresholds
notes: 2025-02-18 meeting: agreed to prioritize per-route error-budget badges before full attribution; trade-off: will delay advanced ML attribution to next cycle
Trade-offs discussion: heavier instrumentation increases cost; initial implementation will sample 5% of traces for attribution signals
Decision log: use a rules-first approach (heuristics) and stage ML-based attribution post-MVP (Q3)
Pilot scope: Payments (high priority) and Search (model-heavy) selected to cover infra and model-regression cases
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (MVP): wire badges + manual advisory alerts to pilot teams (2 weeks). Phase 2: controlled canary auto-throttle for canary cohorts (3 weeks). Phase 3: auto-rollback policy for all canaries and documented runbook (2 weeks). Each phase gated by retrospective and SLO smoke tests.
monitoring: Expose metrics: lighthouse.attribution.confidence, lighthouse.error_budget.burn_rate, lighthouse.rollout.actions.count. Alerts: burn-rate > 2x expected for 5m (warning), error-budget remaining < 10% (critical). Annotate dashboard with last-mitigation and last-rollback events.
mitigation: If attribution confidence is low (<0.5), default to advisory mode and require manual PM/SRE approval for rollback. Implement 'safe-mode' that disables auto-rollback globally if false positives exceed threshold during the pilot.
